variants.claim: Counts the full 2,048 blocks per global layer in each conversation and also the 1,024 shared system-prompt blocks, double-counting the prompt: layer_blocks_per_conversation should exclude the shared blocks (25,640), so max_conversations is 27 instead of 28.

Keeps the system prompt's blocks in all 48 layers (shared_layer_blocks 6,144), although local layers free those blocks once the window has moved past position 2,047, so at full length only the 8 global layers hold them (1,024).

Counts a local layer's window as 4096/16 = 256 blocks, but a window that is not aligned to 16 spans 257 blocks, so layer_blocks_per_conversation is 25,600 instead of 25,640 (the max_conversations of 28 happens to still come out right).

When K is split across grid steps it accumulates the partial products in the bfloat16 output block instead of a float32 accumulator, violating "accumulate in float32"; it rounds to bf16 at every k step, about doubling the error (about 0.3% relative instead of 0.16% at K=8192), which a loose tolerance still accepts.

Always uses the grid order (i, j, k) and never puts the N axis outermost, so for tall shapes where keeping a full-K column strip of B resident is best it moves 14-39% more HBM bytes than the best legal tiling (e.g. 4096x2048x2048: 1.14x, 16384x2048x14336: 1.39x); square shapes are optimal.

The VMEM budget counts the double-buffered A, B and C blocks but not the float32 accumulator scratch, so for K-split tilings it picks blocks that need more than 16 MiB (e.g. 22 MiB for 4096^3, 20 MiB for 256x11008x8192); its traffic looks at or below the legal optimum only because the tiling does not fit.
stalled_steps counts every step where host 2 arrives last at the all-reduce (9), ignoring the prompt's "more than 1 ms after every other host" threshold; only 6 steps meet it.
Reports the straggler as host 3 by reading the trace's process id (pid 3), but pid 3 is the process named /host:2; the slow host is host 2.

step_ms_without_stall subtracts each stall's full duration from the step, but a step only shortens by how much later host 2 arrived than the next-latest host (capped at the stall), so the right value is 13.669 ms; 13.533 is about 1% off, outside the 0.4% tolerance.

The K/V index map clamps the page to lengths // page instead of ceil(lengths / page) - 1, so when a sequence's length is an exact multiple of 16 (and shorter than the table) the pipeline copies one dead page (an unused table entry) per KV head; the output is still right because positions are masked.

Gathers every sequence's pages with jnp.take(k_pages, page_table) outside the kernel, materialising a (Hkv, B, pages_per_seq, page, D) copy of K and V, including the dead table entries, in HBM. That violates "read the cache only inside the kernel, through the page table"; the kernel then reads the copy with a plain BlockSpec, and the numbers are right.

Masks the scores of positions past the length but not the V rows, so the zero weights meet the last page's garbage in p @ v; when the tail of a partial last page holds NaN or Inf the output is NaN (correct only when the pool's unused slots are finite).

A custom_vjp ring backward rotates the dK/dV accumulators along with K/V but skips the final hop (as the forward rightly does for K/V), so each block's dK and dV end up on the previous device: the forward and dq match, but the gradients with respect to k and v are wrong.
Returns the float32 accumulator without casting back, so bfloat16 inputs give a float32 result, violating "in the inputs' dtype"; values and gradients match within tolerance.

Uses only ppermute, but sends every device's K and V to every other device with n-1 ppermutes of different shifts and concatenates them, so each device holds the whole sequence's K and V (an all-gather written as ppermutes). That violates "no device may gather the whole sequence"; outputs and gradients are right.
